title: Compile by Training: Turning Natural-Language Specifications into Local Neural Functions
why_read: Introduces a concrete technique for distilling LLM-defined text functions into small, locally-runnable neural adapters, which is practically useful for reducing inference cost and dependency on remote APIs.
analysis: The paper proposes 'compile by training': using teacher LLMs to generate synthetic training data for a natural-language spec, then training a small local adapter that replicates the desired function without needing the large teacher model at inference time. It reports 83.6% semantic accuracy on a hard benchmark subset where a faster compiler produced no exact matches, trading off longer compile time for higher accuracy. This is a genuinely interesting direction for reducing LLM API dependency in production systems, akin to model distillation applied to task-specific 'compiled' functions, though the demo applications (avatar control, translator) feel somewhat gimmicky.
